headlines.article_text: Amazon-Decart AI software deal Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Amazon has agreed to acquire AI startup Decart's key software and three cofounders, along with much of its top talent, the company announced. Founded in 2023, the Israeli company is best known for its software that lets developers sync their AI models across different chips. It marks the latest example of major tech companies acquiring pieces of buzzy AI startups. In this article AMZN Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT Amazon logo on brick office building facade with windows, San Francisco, California, Aug. 29, 2025. Smith Collection | Gado | Archive Photos | Getty Images Amazon is scooping up much of the technology and talent behind artificial intelligence startup Decart, marking the latest reverse acquihire deal by a major tech company. In a Monday blog post , Amazon said it agreed to purchase Decart's "proprietary technology" and hire the startup's three founders, as well as their AI researchers and engineers. The Israeli startup, founded in 2023, is best known for its software that lets developers sync their AI models across different chips, allowing them to switch hardware quickly, known as the Decart Optimization Stack. "Every leap forward in AI starts with getting more out of every chip," Peter DeSantis, a senior vice president at Amazon who oversees foundation models, custom silicon and quantum computing development, said in a statement. "More efficient compute means better training, better reinforcement learning, faster inference, and better models for customers at a lower cost." DeSantis added, "From our earliest work with Decart, we knew they were the kind of technologically fearless team who would help us push it even further." Amazon has positioned its Trainium and Inferentia chips as lower-cost options for AI developers. Last month, Amazon CEO Andy Jassy said the company plans to make its Trainium chips externally available for the first time in "late in 2027." Several outlets reported Amazon will pay $7.5 billion for Decart's assets, citing people familiar with the matter. Amazon declined to comment on the terms of the deal. Anthropic had considered acquiring Decart and conducted due diligence, but ultimately walked away from a deal, Bloomberg reported. Tech companies including Microsoft , Meta and Google have announced a series of deals with buzzy AI startups, which involve licensing their technology or nabbing their top talent and founders. The moves, often referred to as reverse acquihires , stop short of buying the companies outright. Amazon made two similar deals in 2024 when it brought on talent from Adept and Covariant . The arrangements have attracted regulatory scrutiny in some cases.
